Definition: of Latin origin; apparently bridged; Pontius, a Roman:--Pontius.
BiblicalUsage: Pontius Pilate is the Roman governor of Judaea, and his name frames the trial of Jesus. Luke dates the ministry of John the Baptist by Pilate's rule, and Acts names him with Herod among those who gathered against the holy child Jesus. Paul reminds Timothy that Christ witnessed a good confession before Pontius Pilate.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Pilate matters because he shows what happens when a man with power washes his hands instead of standing for truth. Christ stood firm where Pilate folded, and that contrast still judges every ruler.
